summary: Rechecked all 204 targets across 45 layers, 182 citation occurrences and 109 overlap claims. Two findings: K(S,n) is incorrectly identified with S-unit power classes, dropping class-group torsion (high); the Amice-transform equivalence is incorrectly described with Q_p rather than Z_p coefficients (medium). The broad missing-work verdicts and existing built components remain supported.
checked: Independence and input: read the whole bot-confirmed issue, accepted AUDIT-27 result, REV-AUDIT-27 report, ledger and all five complete roadmap documents at explorer snapshot 6d466a3a0cef4c949493af7c16a3cb3d671d57a9. The completed audit was by claude4/2 and accepted review by claude2/2; neither was this Codex session. This is an attack on that library audit, not a new primary-source extraction for all five programmes.

Coverage: all 45 assigned native layers and all 204 targets were checked: PeriodsAndSpecialValues 10 layers/42 targets, RankZeroOneBSD 12/57, SelmerIwasawaCohomology 5/27, SpecialValuesBirchTate 8/37, ArithmeticKTheory 10/41. The accepted target counts are 142 absent, 57 partial, two Mathlib, two Tau Ceti and one both. Later KU readiness checkpoints are outside the assigned batch.

Read all 182 citation occurrences, including related citations attached to absent targets, with their actual namespace and variable context: 142 distinct declarations in 76 files. Every cited file byte-matches Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174 or Tau Ceti f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369. Additionally checked the uncited S-integer Selmer exact sequence used in finding 1. No Lean compilation was run.

PeriodsAndSpecialValues: checked abstract Hodge filtration/conjugation/Tate twist versus geometric Betti/de Rham realization, top exterior powers and determinants versus perfect-complex lines, completed Dirichlet/Riemann/modular L-functions and normalizations versus motivic algebraicity, formal periods/torsors, unit regulators versus higher regulators, local corrections, K1/SK1 and zeta elements, certified period evaluation, Gauss–Manin/Picard–Fuchs and the quintic/K3 examples, multiple-zeta iterated integrals/shuffle/stuffle and motivic coactions. Searched declarations first and then both source trees under these concepts and aliases. Existing Hodge conjugation is not the Betti F-infinity operator; existing Bernoulli/Riemann values do not prove all Dirichlet algebraicity.

RankZeroOneBSD: checked formal Euler products versus entire modular continuation, analytic vanishing orders, Mordell–Weil finite generation and normal forms, point base change/quadratic-twist descent versus the rank/trace and Sha packages, Néron–Tate pairing normalization and regulator basis independence, explicit 2-descent versus general cohomological Selmer groups, all named nonvanishing/Gross–Zagier/Kolyvagin/Kato/prime-part branches, rational defect valuation reconstruction, certified exceptional-prime assembly and named-curve checks. Searched named theorems and conceptual aliases. Retained the built Mordell–Weil and torsion-pairing inputs; no formal elliptic L-function was treated as analytic continuation.

SelmerIwasawaCohomology: checked canonical all-degree continuous cohomology against the explicit discrete-module low-degree model; H0-only canonical comparison versus discrete-group H1/H2 comparisons; finite-quotient colimit in degree one; inflation–restriction versus full Hochschild–Serre/transgression; cup/corestriction/projection and Shapiro degree and subgroup hypotheses; finite-level Kummer injection versus surjectivity and integral limits; Mittag–Leffler set/tower results versus derived lim¹; Pontryagin and character modules versus arithmetic duality; Selmer local conditions and mapping fibres; completed actions, Amice coefficients, Iwasawa control and Bloch–Kato local maps. Findings 1 and 2 are precise exceptions to otherwise supported classifications.

SpecialValuesBirchTate: checked twisted W2 versus ordinary roots of unity, absent K2/tame kernels and the independent Q example, Dedekind-zeta convergence and residue versus continuation at negative integers, sign and rational all-prime reconstruction ingredients, Tate comparison and Euler-factor removal, odd-prime and dyadic main-conjecture dependencies, S-integer signs, and higher regulator refinements. Arithmetic Bernoulli-prime convention is not the topologists’ sequence. The cited torsionOrder_dvd_absNorm_sub_one carries a coprimality hypothesis; in the relevant totally real, odd-prime setting the roots-of-unity order is two, so this was not turned into a spurious counterexample outside the stated setting.

ArithmeticKTheory: checked S-integer Dedekind/class-group and units infrastructure, K0 versus higher K, rank/determinant and arithmetic K1 gaps, localization and finite support versus odd-degree isomorphisms, Quillen finite generation and Borel ranks, Tate-twisted invariants versus the ordinary roots-of-unity group, odd-group extension data and real dyadic rows, even groups/tame/wild kernels, regular-prime/Bernoulli criteria and certified examples. Searches in both libraries distinguish existing class-group/unit calculations from the absent higher K-theory and arithmetic Chern/regulator comparisons.

Overlap verification: read all 109 duplicate notes and the full descriptions of their 78 distinct stage endpoints, including upstream EllipticCurves and ProfiniteCohomology, ArithmeticGaloisDuality, the main-conjecture and Euler-system suppliers, motivic comparisons and low-degree K-theory. Checked native stage-edge context, reserved IDs and retirements. Every named endpoint is current. Explicit imports and specialization adapters were not promoted to new duplicate findings solely because both layers mention the same object.

Consistency and negative-search discipline: the 45 native assigned layers equal the audited layer set; every target note/status, layer verdict and duplicate list agrees with reviewed library-coverage, including its evidence cap. Index-first and whole-source searches cover all wholly absent targets and missing portions of partial ones, with actual statements read for plausible positive hits. Homonymous Quillen/model-category, presheaf-plus, Coxeter-Matsumoto, probabilistic Bernoulli/hypergeometric and group-action Iwasawa entries were not counted as arithmetic implementations. No finding rests only on a failed name search.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-27.result.json: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L0, target "Integral Kummer comparison H^1(F, Z_p(1)) = lim_m F^x/(F^x)^{p^m}", final sentence of note
findings.claim: The note identifies K(S,n) with S-units modulo nth powers. This drops the S-class-group n-torsion quotient. The cited selmerGroup is the subgroup of field power classes with valuations divisible by n outside S; S-unit power classes form a possibly proper subgroup. The added description as the target of the S-restricted Kummer map also obscures the direction of the cited Kummer injection, whose target is H¹.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174/Mathlib/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SelmerGroup.lean#L163 defines the carrier by ∀ v ∉ S, valuationOfNeZeroMod n x = 1 in the quotient valuation group. It does not require an S-unit representative. At the pinned Tau Ceti commit, https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/RingTheory/DedekindDomain/SInteger/SelmerGroup/Basic.lean#L154 defines fromSUnitLift from the quotient of S.unit K by its nth powers; fromSUnitLift_injective at line 186 proves injectivity; ker_toClassGroup at line 269 identifies its image with the kernel of toClassGroup; range_toClassGroup at line 296, under [NeZero n], identifies the image of toClassGroup with the kernel of nth power on ClassGroup (S.integer K). Thus the existing declarations give 1 → O_S×/(O_S×)^n → K(S,n) → Cl(O_S)[n] → 1, rather than the asserted identification. https://github.com/CBirkbeck/TauCeti/blob/f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369/TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisCohomology/Kummer.lean#L276-L299 defines kummerClassMap from field power classes to explicit H¹ and proves it injective. All these statements and their variable hypotheses were read at the pins; the extra Selmer exact-sequence file was also byte-checked against its pinned blob.
findings.fix: Keep this target partial and preserve the already-correct finite-level Kummer injection/kernel evidence and missing p-adic-limit comparison. Replace the final sentence by the valuation-divisibility definition of K(S,n), record the existing S-unit/class-group exact sequence for n ≠ 0 with the three cited declarations, and distinguish the map of power classes into H¹ from the algebraic S-unit map into K(S,n). An identification with S-unit power classes needs trivial Cl(O_S)[n]. Qualify any nearby use of "S-unit Selmer group" consistently. Reuse the proved exact sequence; do not plan it again or claim an S-restricted cohomological comparison merely from the algebraic sequence.

findings.where: research/blueprint/audit/AUDIT-27.result.json: SelmerIwasawaCohomology:L3, first target, note describing AbstractMeasure.amiceTransformEquiv
findings.claim: The note says the cited Amice-transform equivalence identifies Q_p-valued measures on Z_p with power series. The equivalence at the pin is for Z_p-valued measures and Z_p[[X]]. The generic transform is only a linear map; its extension to an equivalence over general coefficient rings is explicitly left open. This is a coefficient-domain error in the library input used for integral Iwasawa theory.
findings.evidence: https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174/Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/AmiceTransform.lean#L156 gives exactly amiceTransformEquiv : D(ℤ_[p], ℤ_[p]) ≃ₗ[ℤ_[p]] ℤ_[p]⟦X⟧. Its preceding documentation specifies ℤ_[p] coefficients and says generalization requires bounded power series over a normed ring. The generic amiceTransform at line 75 has type D(ℤ_[p], R) →ₗ[R] R⟦X⟧, not an equivalence. The source introduction lines 22–33 makes the same distinction. Both declarations and their surrounding hypotheses were read at Mathlib 082e2d3.
findings.fix: Replace Q_p by Z_p in the equivalence claim and give its actual linear-equivalence type. If mentioning Q_p-valued measures, cite only the generic transform map and retain the missing bounded-power-series equivalence. Keep the target absent: the cited linear equivalence supplies neither the completed-group-ring/cohomology identification nor control, characteristic-ideal or general Gamma-module theory. No new roadmap owner or change of the layer verdict is needed.
